verses.mystical_translation: Blessed is the man that walks not in the counsel of the patterns rooted in harm, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of the scornful.
But his delight is in the law of the the Living Presence; and in his law does he meditate day and night.
And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that brings forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatever he doeth shall prosper.
The patterns rooted in harm are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.
Therefore the patterns rooted in harm shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the aligned with truth.
Contemplatively, this verse gives voice to the longing that violence, deceit, domination, and fear lose their power; it is not a directive against human enemies.

contemplative_note: Rooted attention reshapes a life slowly, like water feeding a tree.
safety_note: Faithfulness is not a guarantee of wealth, health, or easy outcomes; “prosper” is poetic wisdom, not a prosperity formula.
